messages:
Alex H: quick thread — bringing up the new llama-mini-v2 with q8 quant. Throughput looks excellent on h100 but we're seeing a 30–40ms tail latency bump in eu-west and a small quality hit vs flashv3 on the same instance. Anyone seen region-specific weirdness? :thinking:
Ria C: can you drop the perf numbers and the exact runner flags?
Alex H: sure — batch=1 stream, seq=1024, run on p4d and h100. h100 avg token=7.2ms, p99=18ms in us-east. eu-west p99=55ms. throughput (tokens/s) h100 ~1200, p4d ~420. quality: rouge-like eval drops ~1.8 points when switching from flashv3 kernels to triton-q8.
Sam T: interesting. are you using flashv3 q8 kernels or the mixed vendor libs for q8?
Alex H: by default we ran with runtime kernel selector -> preferred: flashv3, fallback: triton. For the q8 path it fell back to vendor-lib-qtk on some hosts in eu-west.
Marta P: vendor-lib-qtk had a micro-patch in EU region infra last week. ops rolled it to eu-west GPU nodes (rolling update). Could be unrelated but worth checking.
Lee W: region skew often maps to instance types + PCIe/NUMA layout. eu-west cluster uses a different AMI + NCCL config, sometimes causes KV cache thrash on 1k+ seq.
Ria C: can you share the exact perf command you used? I can re-run on our infra.
Alex H: pasted run below:
```
python bench_runner.py --model llama-mini-v2 --kernel-selector=flashv3,triton,vendor --quant=q8 --batch-size=1 --seq-len=1024 --profile --region=eu-west
```
Ria C: thanks. I'll run the same in us-west and eu-west and swap the kernel ordering to force flashv3 first. vs forcing triton.
Sam T: quick theory: flashv3 q8 has a smaller working set and relies on continuous batching heuristics. If eu-west nodes have slightly different tail-request distribution (more microbursts) the batching heuristics could create longer queues, inflating p99. Triton might have different scheduling (more predictable p99 but lower throughput).
Marta P: +1. Also check CUDA runtime versions. vendor-lib-qtk is pinned to 12.3 in eu-west AMI; our h100 fleet in us-east is 12.4. There was an alignment bug in 12.3 that affected async memcpy pacing.
Alex H: good call. I'll capture `nvidia-smi -q` and runtime.
InfraBot: deploy: rolled vendor-lib-qtk v2.1.4 to eu-west-gpupool at 2024-06-18T09:12:03Z (ctx: infra-rolling-347). :rotating_light:
Lee W: can you rerun with `--kernel-selector=flashv3!` (force flashv3 no-fallback) and `--cuda=12.4`? if p99 drops then it's a vendor or cuda mismatch.
Alex H: started forced run now. small note: flashv3 q8 on h100 gave slightly worse rouge but identical logprobs for short prompts. So quality regression might be distributional.
Ria C: I'll also throw in a triton-only run and a flashv2 run for comparison. different kernels can change numerical ordering on quant, so check ngram evals too.
Sam T: If you get persistent p99 issues on flashv3 in eu-west, we should consider adding a region-aware kernel override: prefer triton for eu-west until we patch AMIs. Also add a safety net to fallback to triton on live requests if p99 exceeds threshold.
Marta P: can someone open a short incident with steps to reproduce + links to bench artifacts and region node AMI diff? I'll coordinate with infra to hold the vendor-lib rollout.
Alex H: created ticket INF-6421 with artifacts URL and the bench logs.
Lee W: and add a small microbench script to reproduce KV-cache thrash locally: 5 parallel clients, seq=1024, random prefix lengths. I have a snippet.
Ria C: sending snippet in #eng-ml-tests, will paste here too.
Ria C: ```
# micro stress
for i in {1..5}; do nohup python bench_runner.py --model llama-mini-v2 --kernel-selector=flashv3 --quant=q8 --batch-size=1 --seq-len=1024 &
done
```
Sam T: thanks. next steps: (1) Alex rerun forced flashv3 on eu-west with CUDA=12.4, (2) Ria reproduce across regions, (3) Marta hold vendor rollouts until we confirm, (4) if p99 doesn't improve, add region kernel override + tracing hooks to the selector.
Alex H: copying results as they land. thanks all :thumbsup:
Marta P: :eyes:
